title: A year-old Superior level gave no clear six-month Michigan-Huron forecast gain at 1970-2024 issues
abstract: We tested whether a twelve-month-old Lake Superior level adds six-month Michigan-Huron forecast information after current local level and twelve local monthly changes. At 660 monthly issues in 1970-2024, it gave a -0.65% mean squared error reduction. The conditional 95% five-year block interval was -1.43% to 0.12%. Adding current Superior level to that model gave a 6.45% point reduction, with limits of -0.61% to 12.41%. Both primary tests gave no clear gain. Current-only information reproduced the earlier 5.54% campaign point gain. Old values at 3, 6 and 24 months also gave intervals across zero. A ten-year block rule gave a positive current-added interval, so that result depends on the block rule. Revised records, model form, omitted weather and regulation, and conditional uncertainty limit inference. This is a test of observation age in one forecast model, not a physical travel-time estimate. Code, aggregate evidence, exact source hashes, a figure and audits are included. External observations and monthly predictions remain outside the signed package.

display.caption: Old Superior levels added to local history, and current level added to old-level models. Points show MSE reduction in 660 six-month forecasts at 1970-2024 issues. Lines show conditional 95% intervals from 60-month circular blocks. Twelve months is the primary age; other ages are secondary. Positive values mean lower error.
